data.narrative:
Tonbo Imaging, a Series D defense and security company that has raised $66.5M to date, is valued within a frontier-tech sector populated by 2 public comparables (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS) and 8 private peers including Helsing, Saronic, Chaos Industries, and Onebrief.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the $66M total raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.5x multiplier typical of Series D advancement, implies a $100M valuation. Peer-median benchmarking across four same-sector, same-stage comparables yields a $6.9B implied value, with the peer set ranging from $2.1B (Onebrief) to $18.0B (Helsing).

The triangulated analysis supports a broad valuation range of $85M to $7.9B, with a median of $3.5B. The material spread reflects inherent uncertainty in this segment: early-stage defense companies exhibit wide performance variance, and peer valuations span more than an order of magnitude. Stage-progression anchors a floor near deployed capital, while peer-median reflects market pricing for similar-stage competitors. Key sensitivities include technology differentiation relative to the peer set, customer concentration in defense procurement cycles, and regulatory pathway clarity. Further diligence on revenue trajectory, customer contracts, and technical defensibility would narrow this range materially.
